subject.title: feat(cron): script payloads behind the trigger gate

question: Should initial cron script payloads retain the proposed 900-second/200-call contract by expanding the shared code-mode executor, or should the public cron contract be capped to the executor’s existing 300-second/128-call limits?
rationale: Either outcome changes the durable public automation contract and resource envelope; the mechanical code change is straightforward, but the intended production budget needs owner approval.

options.title: Cap the initial public contract
options.body: Limit cron scripts to the existing 300-second and 128-call executor bounds, with matching CLI, schema, documentation, and boundary tests.

options.title: Expand the shared executor
options.body: Raise the shared headless executor limits to 900 seconds and 200 calls, with resource-safety tests that cover all existing executor consumers.

recommendation.title: Cap the initial public contract
recommendation.body: Limit cron scripts to the existing 300-second and 128-call executor bounds, with matching CLI, schema, documentation, and boundary tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked design issue and this implementation make steipete the clearest available owner for the script-budget product contract.
